screening_answers.question: Why do you want to work as an AI Product Engineer at Coditude?
screening_answers.answer: The role is how I already work: Claude Code is my main build tool, I build LLM agents, and I like owning a problem from the conversation through design, code, deploy and support. A small, async-first team that decides through documents and PRs suits me. I also like that humans own judgment and every shipped line, which is how I use coding agents.

screening_answers.question: Describe your experience building with LLM agents, and how one failed on you.
screening_answers.answer: I built internal AI agents at a US-based medical-device company, and open-source agent projects: multi-agent-research-crew (planner, parallel researchers, writer and verifier agents on a custom asyncio DAG with retries, timeouts, token budgets and claim-level citation checks), site-to-agent (hybrid BM25 + vector retrieval, cited answers, SSRF-hardened fetching, eval harness) and PageForge. Agents invent claims, so I added a verifier agent and claim-level citation checks in the crew, and in PageForge the AI drafts only from approved facts and a deterministic validator flags unsupported numbers. In site-to-agent, an agent reading untrusted web pages can be steered or abused, so fetching is SSRF-hardened and answers must be grounded and cited. github.com/huss2003

screening_answers.question: How do you use Claude Code or other agentic tools, and where do you take the keyboard back?
screening_answers.answer: I use Claude Code every day as my primary way of building, and I hold the Claude Code in Action and Claude Code 101 certificates plus CCDV-F and CCAO-F from Anthropic. I review every change it makes. I take the keyboard back for schema design, security-sensitive code and payment paths, and I write tests around agent behaviour and money paths. I am happy to drive it live in the interview.

screening_answers.question: Describe your PostgreSQL experience.
screening_answers.answer: In Orbital Surplus, stock is held inside one transaction (UPDATE ... WHERE stock >= qty) so only one shopper wins the last unit, and payment confirmation is idempotent. In my portfolio backend, slot holds are enforced with a partial unique index and the rate limit is Postgres-backed. I have also used Postgres RLS and pgvector. Those two backends have 9 and 10 end-to-end API tests. I treat a wrong query as a customer-visible bug.

screening_answers.question: Tell us about a project you are proud of.
screening_answers.answer: multi-agent-research-crew and PageForge, as agents that cannot quietly lie: both force every claim back to a source or an approved fact and fail loudly when it does not hold. Another is nanoserve, an LLM inference engine I built from scratch (paged KV cache, continuous batching, speculative decoding) that reached 3.1x throughput over sequential decoding in benchmarks. github.com/huss2003/nanoserve

screening_answers.question: Do you have experience with client-facing or consulting-style work?
screening_answers.answer: Not formal consulting. At the US-based medical-device company I built internal tools, including a CRM and AI agents, for colleagues who used them, and I demo my projects such as ai-lead-receptionist to its target users, home-service owners. I am comfortable explaining trade-offs plainly and I write clearly, and I would like to grow into client conversations.

screening_answers.question: Do you have experience with AWS, Redis, Typesense or Datadog?
screening_answers.answer: Not yet. My deployments have been on Vercel, Docker and GitHub Actions. I work in Python (FastAPI, asyncio), Next.js and TypeScript, and I pick up new stacks quickly: I have shipped 30+ projects across web, WebGL, Flutter, inference serving and agents.

screening_answers.question: What is your expected salary?
screening_answers.answer: I am targeting INR 30,000 per month or more. I am flexible on structure; what matters to me is the total package and the work.
